title: Struggling with asset generation for my type of game
author: raygarraty47
selftext:
Hi all,

Working on a game. shop-keeping type. I created all the systems, they are coded, tested and work well. For now, I use placeholder 'shapes' to test the gameplay systems. 

Time to test how fun it is and how's the atmosphere. I wrote whole setting bible document about it, it's big part of the game. But plot and lore is one, I need to do the art now. 

I need rather limited assets for my game. Scope is decent but not in the assets. Whole game happens from inside a shop - imagine hot dog stand for example. You drag ingredients, assemble the order, serve it, receive money.

So the scene from inside is obv very important, and won't change much. Then there is background with few animations, then customers that appear in front of the window. All 2d  with limited animations - rather choppy, not fluid. 

I'm doing some research, asking chat gpt, and I can't figure out what tool is solid to use for generating and animating this type of thing. Anyone please have any directions for me?

So far I'm using Chat GPT to plan etc. I give prompts to Codex and he does coding in Godot.

I'll appreciate any feedback.

comments.author: Xlorem
comments.body:
Art generation is still limited especially for 3D and when it comes to consistency. It also has the largest pushback for what people dislike about AI.

If you still want to do art generation. Tripo ai or blender + MCP for 3D are good starting points to look into

and for 2D there are a lot of sprite generators but getting used to and researching workflows in comfyUI would be the most help since you seem to be focusing on 2D.

replies.author: raygarraty47
replies.body:
Thanks, I'll give it a try! Yes, 2d and limited animations so I figured it shouldn't be that bad yet for now I struggle with finding the right tool. 

I know it's still early days for generating specific style and consistency, but the game I'm making doesn't need that for the most part.

comments.author: the_builder_ai
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/fltdqzt258yh1.gif

Based on your description of "limited animation for 2D assets that doesn't have to be fluid" - ChatGPT should be able to do it. I just prompted it to make and animate a quick register that received money. Is this what you're looking for or something else?

replies.author: raygarraty47
replies.body: Yeah - less cute but yeah. It can throw out animations? I had no clue!

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body:
Yes ChatGPT is really good at 2D - you don't need any other external apps if you already pay for ChatGPT. Just have it generate a picture first. If you like it, have it generate a sprite sheet and tell it to animate.

https://i.redd.it/6p59l6uxc8yh1.gif

comments.author: scarecr0w12
comments.body:
For a fixed shop view, I'd try a layered scene before asking a generator for a complete animated scene. Keep the shop/background, counter foreground, draggable ingredients and customers separate. That lets an ingredient move behind the counter or into a customer's hand without repainting the whole picture.



Make one customer and one order first. Use a rough layout as the reference for camera angle, counter height, palette and where the customer's hands meet the serving window. Generate or draw the parts against that layout, then clean up their edges and test them at the actual gameplay size. A pretty image isn't much use if the food gets lost against the counter or changes apparent size when you drag it.



For the deliberately choppy animation, start with a few controlled poses: idle, waiting, receiving food, reaction. You can swap poses and move a separate arm or head in Godot; you may not need generated video or a full sprite sheet. Check that the face, clothing and proportions stay consistent between poses before making more customers.



That small test should tell you whether your bottleneck is generating the art, cleaning it up, or putting it into the game. I'd choose further tools based on which of those actually takes the time.
